answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a copper-backed stake that is locked while it trades, like a deposit on a terrace that only long-lived, honest participants climb: newcomers start with tiny transaction limits and earn higher limits only through a history of completed, verified work. Each agent signs its work with a unique cipher key tied to that stake, so creating a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand deposits and doing a thousand histories, while honest agents pay once.
